payload.title: Second tablets, the ark, and blessing or curse

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

aliases: the priests who bear the ark
payload.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
payload.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a white woven linen tunic and sash with a blue-violet priestly robe and cloak, plain and clean. Carry the ark's poles on the shoulder.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

payload.name: The plains of Moab
payload.note: Eastern camp across the Jordan where Moses speaks the law and dies, Deuteronomy only.

stages.label: The plains of Moab

quotes.quote: Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.
in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites

stages.text: The plains of Moab: a broad, low valley of dry grassland and scrub east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho and Beth Peor, with acacia, tamarisk and wild shrubs along the river line. Rising to the west, the bare slopes of Mount Nebo and Pisgah, with a flat-topped summit, look over the Jordan valley. Plain tents of goat hair and rough stone walls mark the Israelite encampment; no buildings of note stand in the valley.

payload.name: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
payload.note: The twin mountains in Deuteronomy where blessings and curses are proclaimed; distinct from the Judges Mount Gerizim, which is the same mountain only by name and is kept apart as a separate setting of Jotham's parable.

stages.label: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim

quotes.quote: you shall set the blessing on Mount Gerizim, and the curse on Mount Ebal.
These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people
These shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse

stages.text: Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim: two bare limestone ridges of the central hill country rising opposite each other across a narrow valley. Terraced slopes of olive and fig, scrub of thyme and oak; on Ebal, a plain stone altar and great stones set upright and coated with white plaster, catching the light.

payload.title: Lament of the forsaken sufferer

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.title: King of righteousness and the coming peace

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

payload.name: Judah (kingdom and land)
payload.note: The kingdom or land of Judah as a single place across Nehemiah, Isaiah, Joel, Habakkuk and Zephaniah; all entries describe the same territory, distinguished only by the section context in which they appear.

stages.label: Judah

quotes.quote: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field
its gates have been consumed with fire
some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns

stages.text: Judah: a hill country of terraced slopes, stony ridges and deep valleys, with walled towns and villages set among olive groves, vineyards and grain fields; Jerusalem on its heights with stone walls, gates and a temple, and fortified citadels; cypress, terebinth and cedar on the uplands.

payload.title: Census and birth of Jesus

payload.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
payload.note: Virgin mother of Jesus, betrothed to Joseph of Nazareth; appears in the nativity, the wedding at Cana, the cross, and the upper room. Distinct from Mary Magdalene and Mary of Bethany.

stages.label: Mary, mother of Jesus

quotes.quote: to a virgin pledged to be married to a man whose name was Joseph, of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.
But standing by Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

stages.text: Mary: a young woman of about fifteen to twenty-five years; slender, of medium height and modest build; olive skin of a Galilean Jewish woman; dark brown hair worn covered beneath a veil; calm, deep-set dark eyes and a grave, gentle face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a long blue-grey wrap-cloak drawn over her head and shoulders. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Joseph, husband of Mary
payload.note: Husband of Mary and legal father of Jesus from Nazareth, of David's line, a carpenter who receives angelic dreams; distinct from Joseph of Arimathea and the other Josephs in the work.

stages.label: Joseph, husband of Mary

quotes.quote: Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man
Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?
because he was of the house and family of David

stages.text: Joseph: a man of about thirty to forty years; a sturdy, working build with strong, calloused hands; olive-brown skin weathered by sun and work; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard with some early grey; a steady, careful, gentle face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown beneath a dark brown woollen cloak. Signature prop: a carpenter's adze or wooden mallet carried at his belt.

payload.name: Bethlehem (David's city)
payload.note: Town of David where Jesus is born in Luke; distinct from Jerusalem and from the gate of Bethlehem.

stages.label: Bethlehem (David's city)

quotes.quote: to David’s city, which is called Bethlehem
Let’s go to Bethlehem, now, and see this thing that has happened

stages.text: Bethlehem (David's city): a small limestone town on a ridge in the Judean hills, terraced olive groves and vineyards on the slopes, dry scrub and rocky pasture beyond the walls. Low flat-roofed houses of pale stone clustered close together, narrow lanes, a modest stone well outside the town, and a cave-stable cut into the hillside below the houses.

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.title: Preaching at Thessalonica; Jason seized

payload.name: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)
payload.note: Pharisee from Tarsus who persecutes the Way, is converted on the road to Damascus, and becomes the apostle Paul; told apart from the king by his Pharisee and Tarsus background and conversion narrative in Acts.

stages.label: Saul of Tarsus (Paul)

quotes.quote: The witnesses placed their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
They led him by the hand and brought him into Damascus.
I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees.
But I was born a Roman.

stages.text: Saul/Paul: man in his thirties to fifties, middle height and spare, wiry build worn by travel and hardship. Olive-brown skin, dark hair cropped short, close-trimmed dark beard with grey beginning at the chin. Lined forehead, deep-set dark eyes, strong nose. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark brown travelling cloak with a fringed hem. Signature prop: a worn leather writing satchel and a plain wooden walking staff.

payload.name: Silas (Silvanus)
payload.note: Jerusalem brother and companion of Paul in Acts and the letters, also named Silvanus in the epistles; all four entries are the same missionary companion, so join them into one cluster.

stages.label: Silas (Silvanus), missionary companion

quotes.quote: Silas, chief men among the brothers.
Judas and Silas, also being prophets themselves

stages.text: Silas (Silvanus): a man in his thirties, of medium height and sturdy build from travel. Olive skin, dark curly hair cropped short above the ears, a close-cut beard. Calm, steady eyes and a weathered, earnest face. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark brown woollen cloak thrown over the shoulders. Carries a traveller's leather satchel and a wooden staff.

payload.name: Jason of Thessalonica
payload.note: Host in Thessalonica whose house is attacked and who is brought before the rulers (Acts); distinct from the Jason who sends greetings in Romans 16:21.

stages.label: Jason of Thessalonica

quotes.quote: Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.
whom Jason has received.

stages.text: Jason of Thessalonica: a man of about forty to fifty years, sturdy and of middle height, with a broad, dignified frame. Olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard streaked with early grey. Steady, lined face with a direct, honest gaze. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist under a dark brown woollen cloak of ochre-brown. Carries no props.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Thessalonica
payload.note: The city in Macedonia with a Jewish synagogue, visited by Paul and Silas in Acts, addressed as the recipient church in 1 and 2 Thessalonians, and named as Demas's destination in 2 Timothy; all four entries are the same city.

stages.label: Thessalonica

quotes.quote: they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

stages.text: Thessalonica: a bustling Roman port city on the curved shore of the Thermaic Gulf, backed by green hills and Mount Olympus visible far to the southwest. Pale limestone and brick houses climb terraced slopes, with tiled roofs and a grid of stone-paved streets. A Roman forum with colonnades, a stone-built synagogue with a plain facade, and a harbour of moored fishing boats and merchant ships; olive trees and cypresses along the walls.

payload.title: Commissioning of Joshua, the Song, and the sentence on Moses

payload.name: Joshua son of Nun
payload.note: Son of Nun of Ephraim, Moses' aide and successor who leads Israel into Canaan; the same individual across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges (as the deceased) and Hebrews, so no other Joshua is separated from him in this group.

stages.label: Joshua son of Nun

quotes.quote: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
Joshua was old and well advanced in years

stages.text: Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.

payload.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
payload.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

payload.name: Mount Nebo and Pisgah
payload.note: Mountain heights east of the Jordan in Numbers where Balaam views Israel and Moses views the land; distinct from the Israelite mountains and Edom.

stages.label: Mount Nebo and Pisgah

quotes.quote: He took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars
under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is opposite Jericho.

stages.text: Mount Nebo and Pisgah: a bare, rounded ridge of pale limestone rising east of the Jordan in the highlands of Moab, its upper slopes broken by grey outcrops and scattered scrub. Below its flanks the Arabah stretches toward the Salt Sea. On the summit stand low, rough-hewn stone altars and a few dry terraces, with no town or dwelling in view.

payload.title: Roll of David's mighty men

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Abraham justified by faith

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
payload.name: Paul the apostle
payload.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

payload.title: Miraculous catch and call of fishermen

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.name: James son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman disciple called with his brother John in Matthew; distinct from James son of Alphaeus.

stages.label: James son of Zebedee

quotes.quote: James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets.
James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);

stages.text: James son of Zebedee: a man in his late twenties to thirties; lean, strong build from hauling nets; weathered olive-brown skin; short dark curly hair and a close-trimmed beard; steady, earnest eyes and a sun-lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre-brown with a dark wool cloak in faded blue-grey. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: John the apostle, son of Zebedee
payload.note: Fisherman apostle, brother of James son of Zebedee, appearing in Matthew, Luke and Acts; distinct from John the Baptist and John Mark.

stages.label: John the apostle

quotes.quote: in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets
who were partners with Simon

stages.text: John the apostle: young man of about twenty-five to thirty; lean, strong fisherman's build; sun-browned skin; dark brown hair falling to the shoulders, short beard; clear, earnest eyes and a steady, youthful face. Signature outfit: plain undyed linen tunic in earth tones with a dark brown wool cloak, sleeves rolled. Carries a coiled fishing net over one shoulder.

payload.name: Crowd in Luke
payload.note: The mass of people following Jesus, hearing John and being healed throughout Luke.

stages.label: Crowd in Luke

quotes.quote: a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon
A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

stages.text: Crowd in Luke: a typical member is an ordinary adult of Judean or Galilean village life, from young adult to middle age, lean and sun-worn, with olive or brown skin, dark hair kept short or tied back, and a short beard or clean-shaven face; plain undyed linen or wool tunic in ochre, undyed cream and earth brown, with a woollen cloak and a head covering; carries no props of their own.

payload.name: Sea of Galilee
payload.note: The lake of Galilee (also called Gennesaret or Tiberias) where Jesus calls fishermen, calms the storm, and teaches by the shore; the common lake identity across the Gospels.

stages.label: Sea of Galilee

quotes.quote: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers
he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing their nets.

stages.text: Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. Low stone-built fishing villages and wooden fishing boats line the water, with nets drying on the shore. Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.

payload.title: The cherubim and the glory leaving the temple

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

payload.name: Man clothed in linen
payload.note: Heavenly figure who marks the faithful with a mark, scatters coals over the city, and measures the new temple with a reed; treated as one guide throughout Ezekiel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side
Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: a figure of mature, steady presence, neither young nor old; lean and upright build; pale bronze skin with a faint radiance; close-cut dark hair and short beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic and priestly linen sash, plain and unadorned. Carries a scribe's bronze inkhorn at his side and a measuring reed of cane in hand.

payload.name: Four living creatures
payload.note: Winged beings with four faces (man, lion, ox, eagle) who bear the divine throne in Ezekiel 1 and 10; cherubim by alias but not the Psalms angels.

stages.label: Four living creatures

quotes.quote: Out of its center came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: They had the likeness of a man.
their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches.
The appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone.
The form of a man’s hand appeared here in the cherubim under their wings.

stages.text: Four living creatures: adult beings of ageless bearing; each has the likeness of a man in form, with four faces of man, lion, ox and eagle, and four wings. Skin is bronze-gold, burnished like coals; hair fine and flowing; eyes bright as torchlight. One signature outfit: no garment, only the wings and the bright radiance of fire about them, colours of gold, bronze and smoky flame. Signature prop: none, but each bears a wheel like beryl stone beside it.

payload.name: Ezekiel's temple
payload.note: The Jerusalem temple of Ezekiel's visions of abominations and the measured new temple.

stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

payload.title: Judgment on Egypt's Jews

payload.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
payload.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Egypt
payload.note: The land of Egypt where patriarchs sojourn, Israel is enslaved and plagues fall; recurs in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Psalms, Ezekiel, Hosea, Micah and Hebrews as the same land.

stages.label: Egypt

quotes.quote: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen
But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them
for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.

stages.text: Egypt: a long green valley of the Nile flanked by pale desert; broad river channels, canals and reed marsh; fertile black earth fields of barley and flax; date palms and sycamores; mud-brick and limestone cities with tall temple pylons, obelisks and fortified walls; the Delta with its towns of Goshen and Zoan.

payload.title: Saul's body recovered from Beth Shan

payload.name: Philistines
payload.note: The oppressors of Israel and lords of the Philistines in Samson's story; a foreign people, not an Israelite tribe.

stages.label: Philistines (typical warrior of the lords' armies)

quotes.quote: the five lords of the Philistines
thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen

stages.text: Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.

aliases: the valiant men of Jabesh Gilead
payload.name: Valiant men of Jabesh Gilead (burial)
payload.note: The men who recover and burn the bodies of Saul and his sons from Beth Shan; a separate episode from the Jabesh townsfolk rescued by Saul.

stages.label: Valiant men of Jabesh Gilead
stages.text: Valiant men of Jabesh Gilead: men in their thirties to forties; sturdy, weathered build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beards; lined, steady faces. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted with leather, under a dun-brown wool cloak, with period bronze-scaled armour pieces at the shoulders. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Beth Shan
payload.note: Canaanite city wall where the Philistines fasten the body of Saul; distinct from Beth Shemesh.

stages.label: Beth Shan

quotes.quote: they fastened his body to the wall of Beth Shan
They put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth

stages.text: Beth Shan: a fortified tell town rising from the broad Jordan valley, its mud-brick and stone city wall high and weathered, with a gate of heavy timber; the old Canaanite temple of Ashtaroth stands within the walls, pale stone with a raised platform; terraced fields of barley and sycamore fig lie below, with the dark ridge of Gilboa visible to the west.

payload.name: Jabesh Gilead
payload.note: The town in Gilead; destroyed by the other tribes in Judges for not joining the assembly at Mizpah, and in 1 Samuel besieged by Nahash and rescued by Saul, who later had his body recovered from Beth Shan and buried there. Both entries are the same place, distinguished only by the episode each recounts.

stages.label: Jabesh Gilead

quotes.quote: no one came from Jabesh Gilead to the camp to the assembly
Nahash the Ammonite came up and encamped against Jabesh Gilead

stages.text: Jabesh Gilead: a walled hill town in the rugged uplands of Gilead east of the Jordan, its mudbrick and fieldstone houses terraced up a limestone rise. Stone city gate and defensive wall on the approach; olive groves, terraced vineyards and oak scrub on the slopes; a spring below the walls.

payload.title: Defeat of Og and allotment east of Jordan
Laws on homicide, injury, and retaliation
The Levite's concubine at Gibeah

aliases: the husband of the murdered woman
the man from the hill country of Ephraim
payload.name: The Levite husband of the concubine
payload.note: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim whose concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah; he cuts her body into twelve pieces. Not the young Levite of Bethlehem who serves Micah.

stages.label: The Levite husband of the concubine

quotes.quote: The Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered

stages.text: The Levite husband of the concubine: a man in his thirties, lean and weathered by travel, with olive skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard shot with grey at the chin. Calm, grave features and steady dark eyes. He wears a plain woven tunic of undyed wool in ochre-brown beneath a long cloak of dusty grey-blue wool. He carries a traveller's staff of dark wood and a leather bag at his hip.

payload.name: The Levite's concubine
payload.note: Concubine of the Levite from Bethlehem Judah, raped and killed at Gibeah in Judges; distinct from Manoah's wife.

stages.label: The Levite's concubine

quotes.quote: She brought him into her father’s house; and when the father of the young lady saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
the woman his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

stages.text: The Levite's concubine: a young woman in her late teens, slender, of modest height, olive-brown skin, dark hair bound back and covered with a linen veil. Plain woven tunic of undyed wool with a dull red border and a long cloak of rust-brown wool. Simple features, dignified and quiet, with a gentle face. No jewellery beyond a bronze ring.

payload.name: Men of Gibeah
payload.note: The wicked fellows of Gibeah, Benjamites who abuse the Levite's concubine to death; distinct from the Philistines and the tribe of Ephraim.

stages.label: Men of Gibeah

quotes.quote: certain wicked fellows, surrounded the house, beating at the door
They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them, and trod them down

stages.text: Men of Gibeah: adult men of mixed middle age, lean and sun-weathered from village and field life; medium to strong build; warm olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-cropped beards; hard, set faces with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a woven undyed wool tunic with a rust-brown cloak thrown over the shoulders. Signature prop: a plain wooden cudgel carried at the belt.

payload.name: Bethlehem Judah
payload.note: The one town of Bethlehem in Judah, home of the Levite, Elimelech's family, Jesse and David; the same place across Judges, Ruth and 1 Samuel.

stages.label: Bethlehem Judah

quotes.quote: There was a young man out of Bethlehem Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he lived there.
All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said
They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
David went back and forth from Saul to feed his father’s sheep at Bethlehem.

stages.text: Bethlehem Judah: a walled hill town on a limestone ridge in the hill country of Judah, flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses climbing terraced slopes, a city gate of heavy timber and stone where elders sit, olive groves and vineyards on the terraces, barley fields in the valley below, and a well outside the walls.

payload.name: Gibeah of Benjamin (Judges)
payload.note: The Benjamite city where the Levite's concubine is abused and killed and that is the scene of the war against Benjamin in Judges; distinguish from Saul's Gibeah in 1 Samuel by the Judges events of the concubine and the war.

stages.label: Gibeah of Benjamin

quotes.quote: the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin
He went in, and sat down in the street of the city
The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.

stages.text: Gibeah of Benjamin: a fortified hill town of the Benjamite highlands, set on a rocky ridge with terraced slopes. Low houses of mud brick and stone stand close together along a narrow street, flat roofs, and a city wall with a gate. Olive trees, vines and scrub grow on the slopes, with open fields and highways running out of the town.

payload.name: Jebus (Jebusite city before its capture)
payload.note: The earlier name of the same city while held by the Jebusites, before David took it; distinguished by the Jebusite occupation context in the judges entries.

stages.label: Jebus, Jebusite city on the hill

quotes.quote: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.
the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
he rose up and went near Jebus (also called Jerusalem).

stages.text: Jebus: a fortified hill town on a rocky ridge of limestone, with high stone walls of rough-hewn blocks and a strong citadel on the summit; flat-roofed houses of mud brick and stone terraced down the slopes; olive trees and terraced vineyards in the valleys below, a spring-fed water channel at the foot of the hill; a gate tower of weathered stone with dark timber doors.

payload.title: Solomon refuses Adonijah's request

payload.name: Solomon
payload.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

payload.name: Bathsheba
payload.note: Wife of Uriah the Hittite, seen by David from the roof and taken into his household; mother of Solomon, and in Kings she presses David over Solomon's succession. The same woman appears in 2 Samuel, 1 Kings and the psalm 51 heading.

stages.label: Bathsheba

quotes.quote: Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s wife?
Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the earth and showed respect to the king

stages.text: Bathsheba: woman in her late twenties to thirties; slender, upright build; warm olive-brown skin; dark hair worn long, bound back under a plain linen veil; composed, dignified face with level dark eyes and fine straight brows; signature outfit a long undyed linen tunic with a deep blue woven shawl over the shoulders; carries no props alone.

payload.title: Job complains of his friends' deceit

payload.name: Job
payload.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

stages.label: Job

quotes.quote: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

stages.text: Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.

payload.name: Eliphaz the Temanite
payload.note: Oldest of Job's three friends, from Teman; first to speak in the dialogues and recounts a night vision.

stages.label: Eliphaz the Temanite

quotes.quote: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite

stages.text: Eliphaz the Temanite: a man of about sixty, lean and upright; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; short grey-streaked beard trimmed close; deep-set, thoughtful eyes and a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a dark russet wool cloak. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: Bildad the Shuhite
payload.note: Second of Job's three friends, from Shuah; speaks in chapters 8, 18 and 25.

stages.label: Bildad the Shuhite

quotes.quote: Bildad the Shuhite

stages.text: Bildad the Shuhite: man in his middle years, lean and upright, with a dignified bearing. Dark olive skin weathered by desert travel. Close-trimmed dark beard streaked with grey, hair cropped short under a head cloth. Lined brow, steady and sober eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a deep rust-brown wool cloak with a fringed hem. Carries a plain wooden staff of desert acacia.

payload.name: Zophar the Naamathite
payload.note: Third of Job's three friends, from Naamah; speaks in chapters 11 and 20.

stages.label: Zophar the Naamathite

quotes.quote: Zophar the Naamathite
Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,

stages.text: Zophar the Naamathite: a man of mature years, past middle age, lean and upright from desert travel. Dark-brown skin weathered by sun. Short grey-streaked beard, hair cropped close under a head cloth. Lined face, firm mouth, steady eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo cloak over the shoulders. Carries only a plain wooden staff of walking.

payload.name: The ash heap
payload.note: Place outside the city where Job sits, scraping his sores with a potsherd (2:8).

stages.label: The ash heap

quotes.quote: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust

stages.text: The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.

payload.title: Levites: priestly line, singers and cities
Sword drawn and flight

payload.name: The Twelve Disciples (collective)
payload.note: The twelve apostles/disciples as one collective body acting together across the Gospels and Acts; distinct from the individual disciples named within them.

stages.label: The Twelve Disciples (collective)

quotes.quote: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,

stages.text: The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

payload.name: Crowd following Jesus (Mark)
payload.note: The gathered multitude that follows and listens to Jesus in Mark's Gospel.

stages.label: Crowd following Jesus

quotes.quote: A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.
they were like sheep without a shepherd

stages.text: Crowd following Jesus: a typical member is an adult Galilean or Judean villager, aged twenty to fifty; sturdy, weathered build; olive to brown skin; dark hair, short-cropped or tied back, with full beards on men; plain, earnest faces. Signature outfit: a sun-faded undertunic of undyed linen with a brown woollen cloak. Props: none carried alone.

aliases: the place where they went to pray
payload.name: Gethsemane
payload.note: Garden where Jesus prays and is arrested, named in Matthew and Mark; in Luke the same place is called the garden on the mount, on the Mount of Olives, so it is one place with three names.

stages.label: Gethsemane

quotes.quote: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane
They came to a place which was named Gethsemane.

stages.text: Gethsemane: a walled garden on the slope of the Mount of Olives, above the city of Jerusalem. Ancient gnarled olive trees with silver-grey leaves and thick trunks; dry limestone and red earth underfoot; low stone wall with a wooden gate; a press-stone and rough stone terrace; pale rock outcrops at the edge.

payload.title: Hymn to Yahweh the creator

payload.name: Heaven
payload.note: God's dwelling above the earth, where Yahweh sits on his throne and reigns; the psalms and Peter's letter both refer to this same heavenly realm, so both entries belong to one place.

stages.label: Heaven

quotes.quote: He covers himself with light as with a garment. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain.
Yahweh is on his throne in heaven.
For as the heavens are high above the earth

stages.text: Heaven: a vast radiant expanse of high sky beyond the earth, a holy place of pale gold light and deep blue vault, stretched out like a curtain and clouded with luminous white and silver. The heavens are high above the earth, the firmament a clear crystalline dome, with the throne of God set in unbroken radiance and no visible horizon.

payload.title: Amalekites burn Ziklag

payload.name: Amalekites
payload.note: The Amalekite people, an enemy nation that attacks Israel at Rephidim in Exodus, comes against Israel at Hormah in Numbers, and is recalled in Deuteronomy as the nation that struck Israel's weary rear; all three refer to the same people.

stages.label: Amalekites

quotes.quote: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Amalekites: a typical warrior of a desert people, adult, aged roughly twenty-five to forty; lean, weathered build; sun-darkened olive-brown skin; dark hair tied back, short beard kept close; strong, wind-creased face with a steady gaze. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic belted with leather, over it a sand-coloured woven cloak in ochre and brown. Carries a curved sword at the belt and a leather shield as their own props.

aliases: the priest with the ephod who flees to David
payload.name: Abiathar
payload.note: Son of Ahimelech who flees to David with the ephod.

stages.label: Abiathar

quotes.quote: he came down with an ephod in his hand.
One of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David.

stages.text: Abiathar: a man in his thirties, lean and sturdy from years of flight in the wilderness. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard greying faintly at the chin. Calm, grave, watchful eyes and a weathered brow. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a dark blue woollen cloak. Carries the linen ephod folded over his arm or shoulder.

payload.name: Elders of Judah
payload.note: Towns and elders of Judah who receive David's gifts of plunder; not the same as the national elders of Israel.

stages.label: Elders of Judah

quotes.quote: he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, even to his friends

stages.text: Elders of Judah: mature men, aged roughly forty to sixty; sturdy, unhurried build; olive-brown skin; dark hair and short grey-streaked beard; lined, dignified faces with steady eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under an ochre-brown wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Carry only a plain wooden staff of office.

payload.name: Ziklag
payload.note: The single town of Ziklag in the southern Judah region, given to David by Achish, raided by Amalekites, and a refuge for David; all three entries describe the same place, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: Ziklag

quotes.quote: Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: therefore Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day.
the Amalekites had made a raid on the South and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire

stages.text: Ziklag: a fortified town on a low rise in the southern hill country of Judah, the Negev edge. Mudbrick and fieldstone houses with flat roofs cluster behind a stout gate of timber and stone. Dry terraces, olive trees, vines and scrub of terebinth; wadi beds nearby, pale and dusty under sun.

payload.name: Gibeah of Saul (1 Samuel)
payload.note: Saul's home town and royal seat in 1 Samuel, where Saul is found, anointed and later fights the Philistines at Michmash; distinguish from the Judges Gibeah by its link to Saul and the monarchy.

stages.label: Gibeah of Saul

quotes.quote: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah
under the pomegranate tree which is in Migron
Saul was sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah

stages.text: Gibeah of Saul: a fortified hill town of Benjamin on a rocky ridge in the central highlands. Stone-walled terraces climb the slopes, flat-roofed houses of limestone and mudbrick cluster near a citadel tower at the crest, and a town gate faces the approach road. Terebinth and pomegranate trees grow at the edge of the upper town, with a tamarisk tree in the open ground below, and hills of scrub and olive fall away eastward toward the wilderness.

payload.title: Job challenges the friends and asks for a hearing
